mainTopic: How to handle an animal found near ירושלים that may be a קרבן: רבי יוחנן's method of waiting for a מום, and why a found male is treated as an עולה and not as a תודה, אשם or פסח.
overview: This amud deals with animals found near ירושלים that may have been set aside as קרבנות. רבי יוחנן objects to רבי אושעיא's explanation, because we never tell a person to sin so that he can gain. Instead, he says to wait until the animal gets a מום, then bring two animals with a condition that covers both עולה and שלמים. The גמרא then asks why a found male is assumed to be an עולה. It answers the possibilities one by one: a תודה is covered by also bringing a תודה with its bread, an אשם is ruled out by age or because the special cases are rare, a פסח is guarded in its season and counts as a שלמים out of season, and a בכור or מעשר makes no practical difference. Next it asks the same about found females, which are assumed to be שלמים. A תודה is covered the same way, and a חטאת is ruled out because the found animal is in its second year and an over-age חטאת is rare. For a goat found in its first year, אביי explains חנניא בן חכינאי's ברייתא: the goat is treated like a חטאת and locked away until it dies. Finally, the גמרא begins a new ברייתא forbidding the purchase of an animal with מעשר שני money, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן objects: we don't tell someone to sin for his own gain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן is troubled by רבי אושעיא's explanation, because it would tell a person to do something forbidden so that he can benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן wondered about it: Do we really tell a person, 'Go ahead and sin so that you can gain'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges the explanation that רבי אושעיא gave earlier for how to deal with the found animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא's approach meant changing the status of an animal that might be a קרבן. רבי יוחנן says that even if this can work after the fact, a בית דין would never instruct someone to do a forbidden act from the start. His point is not that the method fails. His point is that we cannot tell someone to use it.

keyTerms.meaning: He wondered about it; he was troubled by it
Get up and sin; go ahead and do something forbidden
So that you will gain or benefit

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan wondered about it:
phrases.notes: "It" is רבי אושעיא's explanation of the משנה from just before this.

phrases.english: And do we say to a person:
Arise and sin in order that you may gain?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּהֵי בַּהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְכִי אוֹמְרִים לוֹ לָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אושעיא's explanation from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's method for handling the found animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A legal method cannot be an instruction to sin, even if the person ends up benefiting.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's method: wait for a blemish, then bring two animals with a condition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says to wait until the found animal gets a מום, then bring two animals and set a condition about which one replaces it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: He waits until the animal develops a blemish, then brings two animals and makes a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן offers his own way to read the משנה. This way does not involve any forbidden act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the animal has a מום, it can no longer be offered, so it may be redeemed. Nobody has to cause a forbidden change in its status. Because no one knows whether it was an עולה or a שלמים, he brings two animals. He sets a condition: whichever type the found animal was, one of the new animals takes its place, and the other is a voluntary offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Until it becomes blemished (from מוּם, a blemish)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's method has three parts: wait for a מום, bring two animals, and make a condition that covers both possibilities.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan said:
He waits for it until it becomes blemished,
and he brings two animals and stipulates.
phrases.notes: The condition: if the found animal was an עולה, one animal replaces it. If it was a שלמים, the other one does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that was just rejected with a method that avoids any sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wait for the found animal to develop a מום, then bring two animals with a condition covering both עולה and שלמים.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: found males are burnt-offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back and quotes the משנה's rule that males found are treated as עולות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Males are burnt-offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the משנה so that it can question it in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes a found male animal is an עולה, because an עולה can only be a male. The next steps ask why we assume this, since other קרבנות can also be male.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt-offerings, which are burned entirely on the מזבח

phrases.english: The Master said: Males are burnt-offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the wording of the משנה to start a new line of questions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A male animal found in this area is treated as an עולה.

steps.title: Maybe the male is a thanks-offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a תודה can also be a male, so why assume this animal is an עולה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is a thanks-offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's assumption by pointing to another kind of קרבן that can be male.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal might be a תודה, then bringing an עולה and a שלמים would not cover every possibility.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is a thanks-offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a found male is an עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תודה can also be male, so the condition might leave out a real possibility.

steps.title: He also brings a thanks-offering
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he brings another animal to cover the possibility that it was a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings a thanks-offering as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he simply adds a תודה to his condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method of making a condition can be widened. He brings one more animal so that the תודה possibility is covered too.

phrases.english: That he brings a thanks-offering as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תודה question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The condition covered only עולה and שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: He also brings a third animal to cover the possibility of a תודה.

steps.title: But a thanks-offering needs bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a תודה must be brought together with loaves of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a thanks-offering requires bread!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer: bringing a תודה is not just a matter of bringing an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה is not complete without its loaves of bread. So it seems the answer in step 5 is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread; here, the loaves brought with a תודה

phrases.english: But it requires bread!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that he also brings a תודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תודה needs bread with it, so the animal alone does not complete it.

steps.title: He brings the bread too
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he brings the bread as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings bread as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers simply that he brings the bread along with the third animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra cost is not a reason to drop the method. He brings everything a תודה requires.

phrases.english: That he brings bread as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection about the bread.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תודה option fails because it needs bread.

steps.title: Maybe the male is a guilt-offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: an אשם is also male, so maybe this animal is an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is a guilt-offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new possibility: an אשם, which is always a male.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם cannot be covered by a voluntary condition the way a תודה can. So this possibility is a real problem for the משנה.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is a guilt-offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the rule in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a found male is an עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אשם is also male, so the found animal could be one.

steps.title: A guilt-offering is two years old, but this one is a yearling
steps.stepSummary: An ordinary אשם is in its second year, while the משנה is talking about a found animal in its first year.
steps.simpleTranslation: A guilt-offering is in its second year, and here an animal in its first year was found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to age: this animal is too young to be an ordinary אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The age of the animal rules out the אשם. So the משנה must be talking about a yearling.

phrases.english: A guilt-offering is in its second year,
and a yearling was found.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אשם question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The found male might be an אשם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a yearling, and an ordinary אשם is older.

steps.title: But a leper's or nazirite's guilt-offering is a yearling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that an אשם מצורע and an אשם נזיר are brought from yearlings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is the guilt-offering of a leper, or the guilt-offering of a nazirite?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the age answer. Some kinds of אשם do come from first-year animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The age answer only rules out an ordinary אשם. These two special kinds of אשם are yearlings, so the problem comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The guilt-offering brought by a recovered מצורע
The guilt-offering brought by a נזיר who became impure

phrases.english: But perhaps it is a leper's guilt-offering,
or it is a nazirite's guilt-offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer about age in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a yearling cannot be an אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some kinds of אשם are brought from yearlings.

steps.title: Lepers and nazirites are uncommon
steps.stepSummary: These cases are rare, so we do not need to worry about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these situations are too rare to change how we treat a found animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We follow what is usual. Since מצורעים and נזירים are not common, we do not suspect that the animal is their אשם.

phrases.english: They are not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection about the leper's and nazirite's אשם.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal might be an אשם מצורע or an אשם נזיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: These cases are rare, so we ignore them.

steps.title: Maybe the male is a Paschal offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a פסח is also a male yearling, so maybe this animal is a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is a Paschal offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises one last option: a קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח is a male in its first year, so it fits this found animal exactly. It is also not rare.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is a Paschal offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the rule in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a found male is an עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסח is a male yearling and is common, so it fits the found animal.

steps.title: A Paschal offering is guarded, and out of season it counts as a peace-offering
steps.stepSummary: In its season, a פסח is watched carefully and would not get lost. Out of its season, it is treated as a שלמים, which the condition already covers.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Paschal offering in its time is carefully guarded. And one not in its time is a peace-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two cases. Near פסח, owners guard the animal closely. At other times, a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In its season, a lost פסח is very unlikely. Out of season, the possibility does not matter, because a leftover פסח has the law of a שלמים, and the condition already covers שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: They are very careful with it

steps.whatToRemember: A found male yearling is treated as an עולה. A תודה is covered by also bringing a תודה with its bread. An אשם is ruled out by age, or because the special cases are rare. A פסח is ruled out because it is guarded in season and counts as a שלמים out of season.

phrases.english: A Paschal offering in its time, they are very careful with it,
and one not in its time is a peace-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פסח question. The list of possible male קרבנות continues in step 14 with בכור and מעשר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the case into two times
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The found male might be a פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: In season it would be guarded and not lost. Out of season it counts as a שלמים, which is already covered.

steps.title: Maybe the found male is a firstborn or a tithe animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the found male animal might be a בכור or a מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they are a firstborn or a tithe animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another possibility for what the found male animal might be: a בכור or a מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור and a מעשר בהמה can also be male, so the found animal might be one of them. These have their own laws, and bringing an עולה and a שלמים in its place does not deal with them. So the rule that found males are treated as עולות seems to miss a possibility.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal, which is holy from birth
Here, animal tithe: every tenth animal, which is holy

phrases.english: But perhaps they are a firstborn or a tithe animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out a פסח, the גמרא tries two other kinds of male animals.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a found male animal is treated as an עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בכור or a מעשר might also be the found animal, and the rule's condition does not seem to cover them.

steps.title: No practical difference, since found animals are eaten only with a blemish anyway
steps.stepSummary: The only special law of a בכור or a מעשר is that it is eaten once it has a blemish. The found animals are treated that way anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law would that matter? That they are eaten in their blemished state? These found animals are also eaten only in their blemished state!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that worrying about a בכור or a מעשר changes nothing in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What sets a בכור and a מעשר apart is that once they get a blemish, they are eaten as they are. The found animals are already handled that way, because they are not eaten until they develop a blemish. So the possibility leads to the same outcome, and there is no need to worry about it.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? (what practical difference would it make?)
A blemish that makes an animal unfit to be offered

phrases.english: For what law would that matter?
To eat them in their blemished state?
These too are eaten in their blemished state!
phrases.notes: "These" means the found animals. They aren't eaten until they get a blemish, so they end up treated just like a בכור or a מעשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the found animal must be treated as a possible בכור or מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The found animals are already eaten only with a blemish, which is exactly how a בכור or a מעשר is treated.
steps.whatToRemember: A found male yearling is treated as an עולה. A תודה is covered by also bringing a תודה with its bread. An אשם is ruled out by age, or because the special cases are rare. A פסח is ruled out because it is guarded in season and counts as a שלמים out of season. A בכור or מעשר makes no practical difference, because the found animals are eaten only once they have a blemish anyway.

steps.title: Maybe the found female is a thanksgiving offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rule that females are שלמים and asks whether a found female could be a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Females are peace offerings. But maybe it is a thanksgiving offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second half of the rule, about female animals. It asks whether a found female might really be a תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה can also come from a female, so a found female could be one. A תודה has its own requirements, so a replacement brought only as a שלמים would not cover that possibility.

phrases.english: The Master said:
Females are peace offerings.
Perhaps it is a thanksgiving offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rule about males to the rule about females
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that found females are offered as שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A female could be a תודה, which a plain שלמים would not cover.

steps.title: He also brings a thanksgiving offering
steps.stepSummary: The finder brings another animal as a תודה to cover that possibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means that he also brings a thanksgiving offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the finder covers this possibility by also bringing a תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as conditions were used to cover other possibilities, here the finder brings an extra animal. That way, if the found animal was a תודה, a תודה has been brought in its place.

phrases.english: That he brings a thanksgiving offering as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a requirement to the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A possible תודה is left uncovered.
steps.terutzMaskana: The finder brings an extra animal as a תודה.

steps.title: But a thanksgiving offering needs bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a תודה must come with loaves of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a thanksgiving offering requires bread!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer: a תודה is never brought alone, because it needs bread with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the finder brings a תודה, he must also bring its bread. Bringing just the animal seems incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread, here the loaves brought with a תודה

phrases.english: But it requires bread!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the finder brings a תודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תודה requires bread, so the animal alone is not enough.

steps.title: He brings the bread too
steps.stepSummary: The finder brings the bread along with the תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings bread as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers simply: yes, he brings the bread too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra תודה is done fully, with its bread. This closes the question of a possible תודה.

phrases.english: He brings bread as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bringing a תודה without bread would be incomplete.
steps.terutzMaskana: The finder brings the bread too.

steps.title: Maybe the found female is a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a found female might be a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it is a sin offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another possibility for a found female: a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת for an individual can be a female. Unlike other offerings, a חטאת cannot be offered as a שלמים or covered by a condition, so this is a serious problem.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is a sin offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a further possibility for a found female
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that found females are offered as שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The female could be a חטאת, which cannot be offered as a שלמים.

steps.title: A sin offering is one year old, but this animal is two
steps.stepSummary: A חטאת must be in its first year, while the case is about an animal in its second year.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sin offering is in its first year, and here an animal in its second year was found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the animal's age rules out a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual's חטאת is brought from an animal in its first year. The ruling is talking about a found animal in its second year, so it cannot be a חטאת.

phrases.english: A sin offering is in its first year,
and here one in its second year was found.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַטָּאת בַּת שְׁנָתָהּ, וְאִישְׁתְּכַח בַּת שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any found female might be a חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling is about a second-year animal, which cannot be a חטאת.

steps.title: Maybe it is a sin offering whose year has passed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the animal might be a חטאת that was never offered and has gotten older.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it is a sin offering whose year has passed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the animal was set aside as a חטאת in its first year, and now it is older.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת that passed its year can no longer be offered, and it is left to die. If the found animal is such a חטאת, it still cannot be offered as a שלמים.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is a sin offering whose year has passed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a second-year animal cannot be a חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חטאת set aside earlier could have aged into its second year.

steps.title: That is not common
steps.stepSummary: An over-age חטאת is rare, so we do not need to worry about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this situation rarely happens, so the ruling does not need to account for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People normally offer a חטאת promptly, so one passing its year is unusual. Like the rare cases in step 11, it can be ignored.

phrases.english: It is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We must worry about an over-age חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is uncommon, so the ruling ignores it.

steps.title: What if the found female is in its first year?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is when the found animal is in its first year.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one in its first year was found, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the second-year case is settled, the גמרא asks about a found female in its first year. That animal really could be a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 21 only works for a second-year animal. A first-year female might truly be a חטאת, so the גמרא needs a separate ruling for it.

phrases.english: If one in its first year was found, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the gap left by step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The law for a found female in its first year, which could be a חטאת

steps.title: חנניא בן חכינאי: a first-year goat goes to a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes חנניא בן חכינאי: a found goat in its first year is for a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: חנניא בן חכינאי says: A goat in its first year is for a sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא saying that a first-year goat is assigned to a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a first-year goat might well be a חטאת, חנניא בן חכינאי connects it to the law of a חטאת. The exact meaning of his words will be challenged in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא quoted in the ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught: Hananya ben Hakhinai says:
A goat in its first year is for a sin offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A first-year goat is connected to the law of a חטאת.

steps.title: Can it really be offered as a sin offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a doubtful animal cannot actually be offered as a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a sin offering, can that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the plain reading of the ברייתא, that the goat is actually offered as a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is only brought for a definite sin. It cannot be brought as a voluntary offering or on a doubt. So the goat cannot actually be offered as a חטאת just because it might be one.

keyTerms.meaning: Can it enter your mind? (that cannot be!)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the ברייתא as saying the goat is offered on the מזבח as a חטאת. The גמרא rejects exactly that reading.

phrases.english: For a sin offering, can that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The word לְחַטָּאת in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חטאת cannot be offered on a doubt, so the plain reading is impossible.

steps.title: אביי: treat it like a sin offering and let it die
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the ברייתא as כחטאת, meaning the goat is treated like a lost חטאת: it is locked in a cell until it dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: Like a sin offering. He puts it into a locked cell, and it dies on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the ברייתא: the goat is handled like a חטאת that cannot be offered, so it is shut away until it dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא means "like a חטאת", not "as a חטאת". Since the goat may be a lost חטאת, it follows the law of a חטאת that cannot be offered and is left to die. This settles the first-year case without offering anything on a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a sin offering (treated the same way)

steps.whatToRemember: For a found male, the other possibilities are covered by conditions (an extra תודה with bread), ruled out (אשם, פסח), or make no practical difference (בכור and מעשר). For a found female in its second year, the replacement covers a שלמים, with an extra תודה and bread, and a חטאת is ruled out by age. A found goat in its first year, which might be a חטאת, is locked away to die.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that even when a found animal cannot be identified, each possible status gets a fitting response. When a possibility cannot be covered by a condition, as with a חטאת, the animal is left to die.

steps.title: No buying an animal with second-tithe money
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one may not buy an animal with מעשר שני money outside ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One may not buy an animal with מעשר שני money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא and quotes its first rule: you may not use מעשר שני money to buy an animal. This line is setting up the rest of the ברייתא, which continues right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני money is not ordinary money. It carries holiness and has special rules for how it may be spent. This ברייתא puts one specific purchase off-limits: an animal. The ברייתא's next lines will explain what happens if someone buys one anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: The second tithe. It is eaten in ירושלים, or exchanged for money that is then spent on food there.
They buy, or one may buy.
An animal, meaning livestock such as cattle, sheep or goats.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think מעשר שני money can never buy food or animals at all. In general it is spent on food in ירושלים. This rule is about buying an animal with it outside ירושלים.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may not purchase an animal
phrases.notes: This is about buying outside of ירושלים.
